_comment: The real config — see holdings.example.json for field-by-field docs.
Filled in 2026-09-20 from the sourcing below. Share counts drift with
every 10b5-1 sale/grant and every SEC amendment, so re-check these
against EDGAR every so often rather than treating them as permanent —
the same bar the rest of this project holds itself to.
musk.holdings[SPCX]: SpaceX and xAI merged into one entity in Feb 2026
(Fortune, 2026-02-02: https://fortune.com/2026/02/02/elon-musk-spacex-xai-ipo-trillion/)
and that entity IPO'd on Nasdaq as SPCX in June 2026 (CNBC, 2026-06-12:
https://www.cnbc.com/2026/06/12/spacex-ipo-spcx-live-updates.html) — so
unlike a typical private stake this one really is a live, quoted
ticker now, not a hand-marked valuation. The 6.4B share figure is
Musk's total economic stake (Class A + Class B + RSUs/options) per a
2026-08 SEC filing as reported by The Motley Fool
(https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/23/a-new-sec-filing-reveals-exactly-how-many-shares-o/):
only 849M of that are the Class A shares that actually trade as SPCX;
the rest is Class B (10x voting, ~85% of total votes) plus RSUs/options.
This follows the same convention Bloomberg/Forbes trackers use — Class B
treated as economically equivalent to Class A for valuation — rather
than the Class-A-only figure, which would silently understate his
stake by roughly 7x (see net_worth()'s own docstring on why a partial
number is worse than none). If Stooq doesn't carry SPCX quotes, price
will come back missing and this worker will skip Musk that pass rather
than publish a stale number — check [quotes] stderr output for that.
musk.holdings[TSLA]: 717,112,739 shares (20.3%), Schedule 13G/A filed
2026-04-23 (https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/TSLA/schedule-13g-a-tesla-inc-amended-passive-investment-disclosure-631d7da19861.html).
huang.holdings[NVDA]: 851,983,603 shares per insider filing as of
2025-10-29 (https://www.gurufocus.com/insider/4375/jen-hsun-huang).
Huang has been selling small blocks under a 10b5-1 plan roughly weekly
since (tens of thousands of shares against an 850M+ base — under 0.01%
per sale) so treat this as slightly high and re-check periodically.
cashUsd/liabilitiesUsd left at 0 for both — no confident public figure
for either (margin loan balances against pledged stock aren't reliably
disclosed in real time); per this project's own rule, omitted/0 reads
honestly, a guessed number doesn't.
icaoHex/tail and mmsi/vesselName are left unset for everyone below —
verifying an aircraft/vessel tail number to a specific person is its
own research task with a higher evidentiary bar (see
holdings.example.json) and wasn't part of this pass.
--- roster added 2026-09-20 (bezos, zuckerberg, ellison, page, brin,
ballmer) — same cashUsd/liabilitiesUsd/icaoHex/mmsi rationale as above
applies to all of them too. Share-count sourcing per person:
bezos.holdings[AMZN]: 950,400,000 shares (8.8%), per Amazon's own annual
proxy filing as of end-February 2026, as reported by The Motley Fool
2026-09-08 (https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/09/08/jeff-bezos-remains-amazons-largest-individual-shar/).
Directly filing-sourced, not derived.
ellison.holdings[ORCL]: 1,160,000,000 shares (40.6%), held through his
family trust, per The Motley Fool 2026-07-29
(https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/07/29/larry-ellison-owns-406-of-oracle-and-has-backstopp/).
Directly filing-sourced, not derived.
zuckerberg.holdings[META]: no single current source gave an absolute
share count, so this is DERIVED: ~13% economic stake (source below) ×
~2.57B total Meta shares outstanding (Eulerpool, 2026) ≈ 334,000,000.
Stake % is distinct from his ~57-60% VOTING power, which comes from
Class B shares' 10x weighting — this app only needs the economic
(valuation-relevant) share count, not the voting one.
page.holdings[GOOGL] / brin.holdings[GOOGL]: also DERIVED, and weaker
than the above — the only percentage breakdown found (6.1% Page /
5.7% Brin) is from a Dec-2022 source, applied here to Alphabet's
CURRENT ~12.23B shares outstanding (stockanalysis.com, 2026). Both
have sold shares gradually since 2022 under standing 10b5-1 plans, so
these are more likely too HIGH than too low — re-verify against a
current 13G/A before trusting these for anything precise.
ballmer.holdings[MSFT]: also DERIVED — ~4% stake (Sportico, 2026,
citing Forbes) × ~7.427B MSFT shares outstanding (GuruFocus, 2026) ≈
297,000,000. An absolute count exists (333,252,990) but it's dated
2010-11-23, 15+ years stale, so the derived-from-current-% figure is
used instead as the lesser of two imprecise options.
socialUrl pass, added 2026-09-21: musk's was already set. huang's was
previously (wrongly) pointed at x.com/nvidia — NVIDIA's own corporate
account, not Jensen Huang's personal one — fixed to x.com/JensenHuang,
corroborated by multiple outlets' independent coverage of his
first-ever post there. zuckerberg's is Threads (@zuck), his
self-reported primary platform these days over X. ballmer's is
x.com/Steven_Ballmer, corroborated by post content (Clippers, MSFT,
personal condolences for Paul Allen) though not in his Wikipedia
infobox. Deliberately still unset for bezos/page/brin/ellison: page
and brin have no genuine account anywhere (Wikipedia carries none;
every findable handle is an unverified impersonator/fan account);
bezos's name search results are likewise dominated by fan/parody
accounts with no independently confirmable verified badge; ellison's
long-dormant @larryellison account was reported deactivated in March
2026. dell/ortega aren't in this file at all yet (see the holdings
gap note above) — dell's is x.com/MichaelDell per the app's own
SeedData.kt, which doesn't depend on this file existing for him;
ortega is reclusive with no account ever attributed to him.
edgarCik pass, added 2026-09-21: each person's own SEC EDGAR reporting-
owner CIK (not their company's issuer CIK — those are different numbers,
e.g. musk's is 1494730, Tesla's is 1318605), verified against each
person's own data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK<n>.json (its 'name' field
matches). Used by edgar_check.py (see .github/workflows/edgar-check.yml)
to surface new Form 4 activity for review — see that script's own
docstring for why it only reports a diff rather than rewriting the
holdings below itself. dell/ortega still aren't in this file (see the
holdings-gap note above), so they have none.
Residence sourcing beyond the obvious/long-stable ones (Zuckerberg —
Palo Alto; Ballmer — Hunts Point; Brin — Los Altos Hills, all widely
and consistently reported for years): bezos and ellison both moved to
Florida in 2026 (Bezos to Indian Creek Village/"billionaire bunker";
Ellison declared a Florida compound his official residence per Yahoo
Finance, 2026, moving from Hawaii). page is left blank — reporting on
where he currently lives was ambiguous enough in this pass (a Jan 2026
Palo Alto Daily Post piece flagged as much) that guessing would break
this project's own rule against it.
icaoHex/tail/mmsi/vesselName pass, added 2026-09-22: this closes the
gap the note above admitted to — these are the same real, publicly
reported and cross-corroborated identities `SeedData.kt`’s bundled
demo has carried since the start (Mode S hexes/tails via multiple
independent aviation trackers plus 2022 press coverage; MMSIs via
MarineTraffic/VesselFinder/MyShipTracking), just never copied into
this file, so the live backend had nobody to actually poll ADS-B/AIS
for — every flight/vessel card was coming back empty regardless of
real air/sea activity. musk/bezos get real Mode S hexes (tailVerified
true); huang/ellison/zuckerberg/ballmer have a publicly reported tail
number too, but no confidently-sourced Mode S hex to go with it —
left unset rather than guessed, so those four still show no flight
card, honestly, same as before. bezos/ellison/page/brin/zuckerberg get
real MMSIs (vesselVerified true); musk/huang/ballmer have no yacht
confidently linked to them in this research pass, so no mmsi for
them. Vessel cards additionally require `ais_listener.py` running as
its own always-on process with an AISSTREAM_API_KEY — see backend/
README’s vessels section — an mmsi here alone doesn’t light one up.

people.name: Elon Musk
people.bio: Born in Pretoria, South Africa. Earned bachelor's degrees in physics and economics from the University of Pennsylvania (1997); left a Stanford PhD program in materials science after two days to co-found Zip2.

people.name: Jensen Huang
people.bio: Born in Taipei, Taiwan. Earned a B.S. in electrical engineering from Oregon State University in 1984, then a master's from Stanford in 1992 while working at LSI Logic.

people.name: Jeff Bezos
people.bio: Born in Albuquerque, New Mexico. Graduated summa cum laude from Princeton University in 1986 with a B.S.E. in electrical engineering and computer science.

people.name: Mark Zuckerberg
people.bio: Born in White Plains, New York. Studied computer science at Harvard College, leaving in 2004 — sophomore year — to run Facebook full-time; Harvard awarded him an honorary degree in 2017.

people.name: Larry Ellison
people.bio: Born in New York City, raised in Chicago. Attended the University of Illinois and later the University of Chicago, leaving school without a degree after one term studying physics and math.

people.name: Larry Page
people.bio: Born in East Lansing, Michigan. Earned a B.S. in computer engineering from the University of Michigan, then a master's at Stanford — where he took a leave from the PhD program in 1998 to co-found Google.

people.name: Sergey Brin
people.bio: Born in Moscow, in what was then the Soviet Union. Studied computer science and mathematics at the University of Maryland, then took a leave from Stanford's computer science PhD program in 1995 to co-found Google.

people.name: Steve Ballmer
people.bio: Born in Detroit, Michigan. Graduated from Harvard with a degree in applied mathematics and economics in 1977, then left Stanford's MBA program in 1980 to join Microsoft as its 30th employee.
